Around 9.30 pm on Sunday, August 23, Sangeetha got a call from her mother M Kalavathi. “I’ll be late getting home, you have dinner and go to sleep,” she told her. Earlier in the evening, Kalavathi had stepped out of their house in Padi Puthunagar of Chennai’s Anna Nagar West Extension to go to church. Less than two hours later, around 11.20 pm, Sangeetha’s phone rang again. This time, it was the Ayanavaram police calling to ask her to identify the photo of a woman they had found unconscious in a rainwater-filled pit. She had “fainted”, Sangeetha was told. That woman, who was later declared dead at the Kilpauk Medical College Hospital (KMCH), was Kalavathi. Passersby had found the 59-year-old woman unconscious in a pit near the Anna Nagar Tower Metro station in Chennai and alerted the police. With the help of the public, they pulled her out and took her to KMCH, where doctors declared her brought dead. items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday refused to interfere with an Allahabad High Court order directing the demolition of around 72 illegal lawyers’ chambers near the District and Sessions Court in Lucknow [ Central Bar Association v. State of UP & Ors ]. A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta refused a request to refer the dispute to mediation and advised the lawyers occupying the unauthorised structures to vacate them peacefully. It also told the petitioners that the encroachments could not be allowed to continue merely because those occupying them held positions in the local bar association. “Where is this offending construction situated? You tell us. You occupy the main road, you occupy the open space inside the court premises, raise unauthorised construction and then say I am elected as the president of the association, I am member of the governing body and therefore I have a right to continue. No. All demolitions have to take place,” Justice Nath said.
